data.description:
Three values that are accepted by a signature and then never read. All three were confirmed against
the code during the 2026-08-05/06 janitor run; the approved remediation is deletion in every case,
because each "wire it up" alternative requires inventing a capability no caller has asked for.

**a. `timeout_s` — `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py:71`**

`_call_with_retry(fn, *args, timeout_s: int = 30, max_retries: int = 3, **kwargs)` declares,
defaults and documents `timeout_s` ("Per-call timeout in seconds (currently advisory for stub-based
callers)", `:86`) but the body never reads it. Six call sites in `apply_outbound.py` (`:101`, `:109`,
`:180`, `:202`, `:227`); none passes it.

The defect is not inertness. Because `timeout_s` is a *named* keyword-only parameter in front of
`**kwargs`, a caller who passes `timeout_s=60` intending it for the wrapped Jira client has it
**swallowed by the wrapper instead of forwarded**. This wrapper is on the path for every Jira write.
Deleting the parameter restores the natural behaviour: `timeout_s` flows through `**kwargs` to `fn`.

**b. `run_eval(dirty=True)` — `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:626`**

Declared, never read in the body; no caller in `src/` or `tests/` passes it (five `run_eval(` call
sites, all in `tests/unit/test_eval.py`). The boolean falsely implies the eval-provenance source can
be switched.

**c. Two permanently-`Unavailable` metric seeds — `src/rebar/metrics/registry.py:136-158`**

`module_size_trend` and `commit_cadence_trend` both carry `compute=_no_data_yet`, which returns
`None`, so `evaluate` always yields `Unavailable`. `accruing_since` is `2026-07-18` with no data
source landed. `git_metrics.register()` registers six entirely different ids
(`module_size_distribution`, `oversized_module_count`, `complexity_summary`, `duplication_summary`,
`churn`, `refactor_to_addition_ratio`), so nothing currently competes for these ids.

The latent trap: every registrar appends under `if spec.id not in existing`
(`git_metrics.py:277`, `event_metrics.py:367`, `bug_trends.py:337`). A future real implementation of
`module_size_trend` would find the seed already holding the id and be **silently skipped** — no
error, no warning, and the metric would keep reporting `Unavailable`. Deleting the seeds frees both
ids so a real spec registers cleanly.

`tests/unit/metrics/test_git_metrics_heldout.py:138-142` (`test_trend_unavailable`) asserts the
placeholder stays `Unavailable` — a change-detector test pinning a stub in place. It goes with them.

Note: no consumer of the two metric ids was found outside the registry and that test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `timeout_s` is removed from `_call_with_retry`'s signature and its docstring `Args:` entry;
      a caller passing `timeout_s=` now reaches `fn` through `**kwargs`
- [ ] `dirty` is removed from `run_eval`'s signature
- [ ] The `module_size_trend` and `commit_cadence_trend` specs are removed from `REGISTRY`, and
      `_no_data_yet` goes too if it has no remaining user
- [ ] `test_trend_unavailable` is removed
- [ ] `rebar metrics` output no longer advertises two ids that can never carry a value
- [ ] No behavior change to Jira retry/backoff, eval runs, or any metric that reports real data
data.title: Delete three accepted-then-ignored values: timeout_s, run_eval(dirty=), two metric seeds
